analysis: Examined the docs/architecture/inference.md head excerpts (lines 798-1636). The only change, at head lines 1370-1382, is documentation describing the Qwen inline MTP assistant. The assistant speculates for one decode row only. While other rows decode, its rows run ordinary chained decode. Target hidden rows are appended to assistant history in step order, and the carry is stored once no successor is in flight. The final prompt row's hidden state serves as the first carry. Opt-in is per drafter (supportsOrdinaryDecodeHistory). The documented rollback switches are DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY. This is a performance and correctness description of in-process decode state. It introduces no new trust boundary, wire field, persistence or cache identity change. Surrounding text (lines 1384-1402) states that complete SSD reuse restores only normalized trusted prompt history and that speculative draft KV is never shared, so T-041 at-rest and salt scoping are unaffected by this doc change. Acceptance remains target-authoritative (lines 1317-1319), so T-007 is unchanged. The new DARKBLOOM_TTFT_* environment keys should fall under the existing DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment rejection of unrecognized or performance-affecting DARKBLOOM_* keys (lines 1145-1147). Integration may confirm that the actual implementation (EngineLoopV2+MTPOrdinaryHistory.swift, finalizeMTPOrdinaryHistory) keeps assistant history request-local, so that no cross-request carry leaks between rows (T-028/A-001). That source is not supplied, and this doc change is not evidence of a regression. No findings.
